title: Saudi Arabia's Covert Air Strikes on Iran in Late March Revealed by Reuters
detail: Reuters broke an exclusive report on May 12 revealing that Saudi Arabia had secretly launched multiple Air Force strikes on Iranian targets in late March 2026, in retaliation for Iranian missile and drone attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure. The operation marked the first known instance of Saudi Arabia directly striking Iranian soil in the modern era. According to sources cited by Reuters, Saudi Arabia privately informed Iran of the strikes through backchannel communications, and both sides then engaged in intensive diplomatic de-escalation to prevent wider escalation. Neither Riyadh nor Tehran officially confirmed the attacks, and Saudi authorities declined all comment. Analysts described the disclosure as a significant watershed — confirming that the Saudi-Iran confrontation had crossed a threshold from proxy warfare to direct military exchange, adding complexity to ongoing ceasefire negotiations.

media.caption: Reuters exclusive: Saudi Arabia secretly struck Iranian targets in late March 2026

title: Saudi FM Prince Faisal Bin Farhan Visits London, Discusses Hormuz Reopening with UK
detail: Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan traveled to London on May 12 and met British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper for substantive talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and strengthening bilateral defense and investment ties. Discussions focused on coordinated international pressure on Iran to allow safe passage for commercial shipping through Hormuz, given the severe disruption to global energy markets. The Saudi FM also held separate phone calls with the Qatari and Jordanian foreign ministers, discussing regional coordination on ceasefire support and humanitarian access to Yemen and Gaza. The London visit was part of a broader Saudi diplomatic offensive to present Riyadh as a stabilizing actor in the regional crisis.

media.caption: Saudi FM Prince Faisal bin Farhan visits London for talks on Hormuz reopening and bilateral ties
